source: Marker definitions and thresholds read by copylint.py. The README summarizes each marker; edit this file and the README together.

markers.name: trailing benefit clause
markers.why: A complete clause ends, then a comma, then a verb-ing tail asserting a benefit. Owners state the fact and stop.

markers.name: fronted participial
markers.why: Sentence opens with a verb-ing phrase before the actor. Actors come first in shop speech.

markers.name: copular abstraction
markers.pattern: \b(is|are|was|were)\s+(all about|designed to|here to|dedicated to|committed to|built to|meant to|about)\b
markers.why: Describes what a service IS rather than what hands do.

markers.name: antithetical polarity
markers.why: not just X but Y. Contrast used for weight where a number or a tool would do.

markers.name: colon then explanation
markers.origin: Common in model-written service copy; refined against false positives on label:value pairs.
markers.why: A claim pre-announced then unpacked. The defect is the pre-announcement, not the colon: a label-to-value colon (Hours: 9 to 5) is fine.

markers.name: symmetrical tricolon
markers.why: Three equal-weight, equal-length parallel clauses built to be read as a set.

markers.name: symmetrical bicolon
markers.why: Two matched clauses joined by and, same grammar, syllable counts within 2.

markers.name: rhetorical question header
markers.why: Question header simulating customer empathy, answered immediately below.

markers.name: agency gloss
markers.why: Abstract-virtue adjectives stacked on a concrete physical task.

markers.name: tagline headline
markers.why: Short abstract headline working as free-standing ad copy, naming no business, place, price, time or service.

markers.name: label with bolted-on claim
markers.origin: Style guidance: a name is the bare noun.
markers.why: A service or section name is the bare noun. No verb phrase, participle, preposition tag or explanation bolted on.

markers.name: flat sentence-length entropy
markers.origin: Common in model-written service copy; thresholds tuned on the corpora in this repository.
markers.why: Four or more consecutive prose sentences whose word-count coefficient of variation is under 0.18 where the mean is 14 words or more. CV rather than raw stdev because stdev scales with sentence length: 3.0 on 12-word sentences is 25% variation and on 24-word sentences only 12.5%. Window widened from 3 because three declarative human sentences hit a low stdev by coincidence (13, 14, 13 gives 0.58). Human copy is bursty. Advisory only: see corpus/KNOWN-MISSES.md for why the threshold is unsized.

markers.name: banned dash
markers.why: Em dash and en dash are banned. The hyphen is permitted.

markers.name: banned phrase
markers.origin: Stock phrases and boilerplate closes common in model-written and template copy.
markers.pattern: \b(quick one|quick question|just a quick|dive in|in today's fast-paced world|it's worth noting|elevate your|unlock (your|the)|leverage(s|d)? (our|your|the)|tapestry|navigating the landscape|game-changer|take it to the next level|peace of mind|one-stop shop|cutting-edge|state-of-the-art|on autopilot|in your words|share (that|your) experience|we would love for you to|thank you for choosing|we value your)\b
markers.why: Named phrase bans: stock openers, filler, buzzwords and customer-service boilerplate closes that signal machine or template copy. Includes 'quick one' and its family, which is filler a small-business owner would not say out loud.

markers.name: determiner tricolon
markers.origin: Measured on labelled sample variants; the clause tricolon M6 cannot see a noun triple.
markers.why: Three parallel noun phrases sharing one determiner: 'your time, your trust, and your style'. The machine isocolon in its commonest form.

markers.name: imperative possessive series
markers.origin: Measured on a labelled scored set; M6 missed it because the clause lengths diverge.
markers.why: A repeated imperative-plus-possessive frame: 'Refine your wardrobe, express your individuality, and command respect'. The tell is the frame, not matched length.

markers.name: noun-phrase tricolon
markers.origin: Measured on a restaurant page whose strapline tripped no other marker.
markers.why: Three consecutive verbless noun-phrase fragments, 2 to 4 words each, at least two carrying an adjective. The machine strapline in its commonest form. M6 sees clause tricolons and M15 needs a shared determiner, so neither can see 'Globally-inspired menus. Welcoming atmosphere. Award-winning hospitality.' A genuine fragment menu carries no adjectives and does not flag.

file_checks.name: no operational boundary
file_checks.origin: Common blind spot of marker-only linters; made structural after vocabulary-list versions were easy to spoof.
file_checks.why: Copy with zero limits, hours, exclusions, deposits, cancellation terms or payment rules reads as an AI simulation of a business with infinite capacity. TESTED STRUCTURALLY, NOT BY VOCABULARY: a keyword list is spoofed by naming a price. A page passes on one of five boundary archetypes (A condition with a penalty, B capacity ceiling, C scope exclusion, D prerequisite gate, E posted schedule). The F1 fixture in corpus/ pins the true and false cases, including a spoof sentence that must not pass.

archetypes.B_hard_capacity_ceiling: \b(only|strictly|exclusively|no more than|maximum of|max(imum)? \d|up to \d|limit(ed)? to)\b[^.!?]{0,60}?(\b\d|\b(mon|tues|wednes|thurs|fri|satur|sun)day\b|\bappointment|\bbooking|\bper (day|week|weekend|month))|\bby appointment\b|\bappointment only\b|\bno walk-?ins?\b|\bwalk-?ins?\b[^.!?]{0,40}\b(only|on (mon|tues|wednes|thurs|fri|satur|sun)day)\b|\bminimum\s+(spend|order|purchase|party|group|booking|of)\b|\b(available|valid|offer(ed)?|runs?)\b[^.!?]{0,40}?\b(jan|feb|mar|apr|may|jun|jul|aug|sep|oct|nov|dec)[a-z]*\.?\s*\d{1,2}\b[^.!?]{0,20}?[-\u2010-\u2015to through until]{1,10}\s*(\b(jan|feb|mar|apr|may|jun|jul|aug|sep|oct|nov|dec)[a-z]*\.?\s*)?\d{1,2}\b
archetypes.D_prerequisite_gate: \b(must|must have|need to|needs to|have to|has to|required to|required|requires?)\b[^.!?]{0,90}?(\b(before|prior to|ahead of|in advance|at drop[- ]?off|when you (drop|bring|come))\b|\b\d[\d,.]*\s*[-\u2010-\u2015]?\s*(hour|hr|day|week|minute|min|month|dollar|percent|%)\w*\b|\$\s?\d|\b(deposit|retainer|permit|proof of|insurance|photo id|valid id|appointment)\b)|\b(bring|provide|supply)\b[^.!?]{0,60}?\b(before|prior to|when you (drop|bring|come))\b|\b(deposit|retainer|fee|permit|proof of \w+|insurance|photo id|valid id)\b[^.!?]{0,60}?\b(is|are)\s+(required|due|non-?refundable|payable)\b

file_checks.name: draft residue in copy
file_checks.why: Builder scaffolding, prompt residue or placeholder text surviving into visible copy, for example a credential card reading 'Her own words on her About page, and the events behind them.'

file_checks.name: asset reused across the page
file_checks.why: One image wired into three or more places on a single page. Reads as a thin library rather than a real shoot.

file_checks.name: monotonous grid rhythm
file_checks.why: The same two-column split declared four or more times, an alternating 50/50 flip down the whole page. The commonest generated-site cadence.
